data.hypothesis: A 2-thread CTA increases the number of CTAs relative to the previously tested 4-thread configuration and could expose more scheduling parallelism. However, its even lower warp utilization and increased CTA overhead may outweigh that benefit; prior measurements were non-monotonic, so the result must be measured rather than inferred.
data.notes: This changes only launch geometry: the kernel, one-thread-per-target mapping, force equations, and memory strategy remain unchanged. The existing search measurements were 0.0018741144478179787 s for 4 threads, 0.0018244869850685304 s for 8, and 0.0017977761749200774 s for 16; they do not establish whether 2 threads will help. Require correctness validation for every supported size before comparing official timings.
transformations: Set block and items_per_block to 2 while retaining shared_memory_bytes at 0; leave src/nbody_kernel.cu unchanged.
